findings.title: Penang destination filter returns service unavailable
findings.severity_rationale: A primary destination filter option fails with a server error, blocking users from viewing that destination.
findings.priority_rationale: Direct user-visible outage on a core browse flow; should be triaged in next fix window.
findings.impact: Users cannot browse Penang inventory despite destination being offered.
findings.expected: Penang properties load (for example The George visible in all-destinations list).
findings.expected_basis: Destination option exists and Penang property cards are present in unfiltered results.
findings.actual: Results unavailable alert appears with HTTP 503 and reference ID.
possible_causes: Penang-filtered backend query path unavailable while general and other destination queries remain healthy.
Service dependency for destination-specific inventory endpoint degraded.
findings.recommendation: Triage backend availability for Penang filter path, add health checks for destination-specific queries, and fail over to graceful empty-state only when no inventory exists rather than 5xx.

findings.title: Account Travel preferences endpoint consistently returns internal server error
findings.severity_rationale: Authenticated account feature is inaccessible due repeated 500 responses.
findings.priority_rationale: Core authenticated account section broken for all observed attempts.
findings.impact: Users cannot view or manage travel preferences.
steps: Observe error; click Try again once.
findings.expected_basis: Account section link and retry action indicate supported feature.
findings.actual: HTTP 500 alert appears on initial load and retry, with distinct reference IDs.
possible_causes: Server exception in preferences retrieval or serialization path.
Required profile/preferences record missing and not gracefully handled.
findings.recommendation: Inspect server logs using UI reference IDs, add null-safe handling for missing preference records, and add integration tests for account/preferences success and retry behavior.
